html:
The Battle of the Plains of Abraham was fought on 13 September 1759 on a plateau just outside the walls of Quebec City, in today's Canada. A British army under General James Wolfe beat the French under the Marquis de Montcalm. Both generals died of their wounds.

It was part of the Seven Years' War, in which Britain set out to conquer New France. Quebec, its capital, stood on cliffs above the St Lawrence River. Wolfe besieged it from June for nearly three months without success. On the night of 12 September his men rowed upstream to a cove and climbed a steep cliff path. By morning about 4,400 soldiers stood in line on the plain. Montcalm attacked at once, without waiting for more troops. The British held their fire until the French were very close. Their volleys broke the French line in about fifteen minutes.

Quebec surrendered five days later, and Montreal fell in 1760. In the peace of 1763 France gave up Canada, which became the British Province of Quebec and kept its French language and faith. With the French threat gone, the Thirteen Colonies needed British protection less. That helped lead to the American Revolution.
